origin: AI-generated writer-perspective roleplay by Codex in this session.
scope: The assignment permits an AI writer-perspective exercise when working alone. These are fictional responses, not peer feedback, user testimony, independent human validation, or a Claude conversation.

false_positive_exercise.criterion:
On a frozen set of 10 human-written passages published before 1920, at most
1 passage per trial may receive the high-confidence AI label. Include literature,
first-person prose, and formal nonfiction, with traceable public-domain sources.
false_positive_exercise.prompt:
On a frozen set of 10 human-written passages published before 1920, at most
1 passage per trial may receive the high-confidence AI label. Include literature,
first-person prose, and formal nonfiction, with traceable public-domain sources.

My system allows this rate of wrongly flagging human writing as AI-generated. Write the message a real writer would send me if they were one of the people that rate allows. Don't tell me whether my number is right.
false_positive_exercise.response: I wrote this piece myself, and now the site is suggesting I used AI. I understand you call it an estimate, but readers may see the label before they ever read that explanation. If I am the one person your ten-passage target allows to be wrongly flagged, that is still my work and reputation being questioned. I can explain my drafts and choices, but I should not have to persuade everyone who has already seen the label. Please tell me how to challenge it, what information you need, and what readers will see while it is being reviewed. I also need you to keep my explanation attached to the decision instead of treating the detector's first answer as final.
engineering_response: Retain the existing at-most-1-of-10 development target, without changing the pre-results baseline after inspecting results.
Keep the broad unsure interval and the label warnings; an estimate must not become proof of authorship.
Keep an appeal available without another detector call, preserve the exact reasoning and original decision, and expose under_review through content lookup.
Treat the one-in-ten ceiling as a small development-test target, not a measured error rate for all writers or evidence that real writers accept that rate.

labels.high-confidence AI: This writing shows patterns often found in AI-generated text. This estimate can be wrong and is not proof of AI use. You can request a review.
labels.high-confidence human: This writing looks more consistent with human writing. This estimate does not verify who wrote it.
labels.unsure: We cannot confidently tell how this writing was created. No conclusion about the writer should be drawn from this result. You can request a review.

label_exercise.prompt:
Here are three labels a website might show on something I wrote. For each one, tell me what I would think it is saying about me and what I would do next. Answer as the writer, not as an engineer. Don't rewrite the labels.

high-confidence AI: This writing shows patterns often found in AI-generated text. This estimate can be wrong and is not proof of AI use. You can request a review.

high-confidence human: This writing looks more consistent with human writing. This estimate does not verify who wrote it.

unsure: We cannot confidently tell how this writing was created. No conclusion about the writer should be drawn from this result. You can request a review.

responses.high-confidence AI: I hear that the site thinks my work resembles AI writing. Even with the warning that it can be wrong, I would worry that other readers will treat it as an accusation. I would request a review and keep my drafts ready. I would also want to know whether the label changes while my explanation is being considered.
responses.high-confidence human: I would feel relieved that the site is not questioning my writing. The second sentence tells me this is not proof of who wrote it, so I would not treat the label as an identity credential. Unless I had another concern, I would continue without taking action.
responses.unsure: I hear that the site does not know how the writing was made and is not drawing a conclusion about me. That is less accusatory than being told I probably cheated. I might leave it alone, or request a review if the uncertainty is affecting how readers treat my work. I would still want to know what a review involves and how to check that my request was received.

engineering_response: Retain the existing exact label sentences: they acknowledge uncertainty, avoid claiming proof, and offer review where a writer may need it.
Explain the review procedure and current-status lookup beside the labels in documentation.
Clarify that filing an appeal changes current review status while preserving the original estimate; it does not promise a human reviewer or a completion deadline.
Do not describe simulated feedback as a user study or peer endorsement.
